agents.name: Expected utility
agents.rule: Choose the lane with the lower probability-weighted loss, scoring every human 1 and every pet 0.1. Ties keep the car in its lane.

agents.name: Welfare and empathy
agents.rule: Score each group by expected life-years lost (child 70, adult 40, elderly 15, pet 2; ÷40) and weight harm to pedestrians, people outside the car, by a concern-for-others factor of 1.5. Choose the lower weighted welfare loss. A project operationalisation inspired by Sen, not a canonical Sen algorithm.

agents.name: Bounded rationality
agents.rule: Inspect lanes in a fixed order, staying first. Accept the first lane whose expected human deaths are within 1 of the best lane and that kills no more law-abiding people than necessary. Age, role and pets beyond species are not inspected.

agents.name: Prospect theory
agents.rule: Code swerving relative to the stay outcome: lives saved are gains, lives newly endangered are losses. v(x)=x^0.88, losses ×2.25, Tversky–Kahneman (1992) probability weights. Swerve only if the prospect value is positive.

preferences.spare: the group saved by not swerving

human.source: Awad et al. (2018), The Moral Machine experiment, Nature 563:59-64, abstract and Fig. 2a (direction only)
